name: Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park
blurb: Cerrado savanna, maned wolves and the fire that shapes the grass.

tip.title: Take away fire
tip.text: Fire renews the grasses and keeps the savanna open. Set Seasonal fire to -100% and watch the grasses, then the deer, rheas and termites that rely on them.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Wet-season rains
nodes.desc: Rain falls mostly in the wet season, and the Cerrado has a strong dry season from about April to September.

nodes.name: Seasonal fire
nodes.desc: Fire shapes the Cerrado, and many of its plants have thick, corky bark or other traits that let them survive it.

nodes.name: Veredas & Rio Preto streams
nodes.desc: Water-table swings, streams and gallery forests give the dry savanna wet refuges. The Rio Preto is the park's main river.

nodes.name: Poor acidic soils
nodes.desc: Cerrado soils are well drained and mostly acidic and low in nutrients, which helps set what can grow.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi and soil microbes break down dead grass, leaves and wood and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Cerrado grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses form most of the herb layer of the open savanna, which Wikipedia says typically reaches about 60 cm. Golden carpetgrass is well recorded here.

nodes.name: Fire-adapted cerrado trees
nodes.desc: Qualea trees dominate much of the Cerrado. Many Cerrado trees have thick corky bark that protects them from fire.

nodes.name: Myrcia shrubs
nodes.desc: Common fruiting shrubs and trees of the Cerrado. GloBI records link their fruit to many birds, tapirs, coatis and foxes.

nodes.name: Wolf apple
nodes.desc: A tomato-like fruit that Wikipedia says can make up 40 to 90 percent of the maned wolf's diet and is available all year.

nodes.name: Buriti palm
nodes.desc: A palm of wet ground that Wikipedia says tapirs, peccaries, fish and monkeys depend on for its fruit. It marks the vereda wetlands.

nodes.name: Termites
nodes.desc: Termites and leafcutter ants are described as main herbivores and decomposers of the Cerrado. Their nests are a food source for anteaters.

nodes.name: Leafcutter ants
nodes.desc: Cut leaves to feed fungus gardens. Wikipedia says nests reach densities of up to 4,000 per hectare in the Cerrado.

nodes.name: Pampas deer
nodes.desc: A Near Threatened grassland deer that eats new growth, herbs and shrubs and follows flowering plants. Pumas and jaguars hunt it.

nodes.name: Greater rhea
nodes.desc: A large flightless bird that mainly eats broad-leaved plants, seeds and fruit, plus insects and small animals. Cougars are its main predator.

nodes.name: Lowland tapir
nodes.desc: Eats fruit and leaves, and GloBI records it eating Myrcia. Buriti fruit is a food for tapirs, and the park lists tapir as present.

nodes.name: Great kiskadee
nodes.desc: One of the best-recorded birds here. GloBI records it eating Myrcia fruit, and it also takes insects and small prey.

nodes.name: Giant anteater
nodes.desc: Tears open termite and ant nests with its claws and licks up the insects. Only jaguars and pumas are known to hunt adults.

nodes.name: Nine-banded armadillo
nodes.desc: Digs for insects such as ants and termites. It is prey for maned wolves, ocelots and big cats in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Red-legged seriema
nodes.desc: A grassland bird that eats arthropods such as ants, grasshoppers and beetles, plus lizards, snakes and small mammals. Common in the Cerrado.

nodes.name: Maned wolf
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats mostly plant matter, especially wolf apple, plus armadillos, rodents and birds. Its dung helps leafcutter fungus gardens and seed germination.

nodes.name: Black vulture
nodes.desc: The park lists black vultures among its birds. They clean up carcasses of animals that have died.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: The largest cat here. Its prey in the Cerrado includes giant anteater, tapir and deer, and it also hunts maned wolves.

nodes.name: Puma
nodes.desc: A widespread big cat that hunts deer, rheas, armadillos and anteaters. It is a main predator of pampas deer.
